proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a returned certificate \(\kappa_H\) and first work on the normalized expansion.  By \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\), for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\) there is a unique \(\eta=\nu_H(\theta)\in\mathcal I_H\) such that
\[
 O_H^N(\eta)=O_H(\theta),
 \qquad
 T_{a,H}^N(\eta)=T_{a,H}(\theta).
\tag{1}
\]

Suppose first that \(\kappa_H=(F_H,\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}},\mathfrak D_H)\).  The accepting computation is finite by \(\textnormal{thm:transition-soundness-termination}\).  Induct over its transition log.  The induction invariant is that every current labelled kernel is the normalized structural kernel represented by that label and that each displayed rational equality is valid after multiplication by the product of the divisors already entered in the ledger.  The base is the normalized observation kernel \(o_H^N(\eta)\).  The context step preserves the invariant by evaluating a known zero--one selector multiplexer at a value \(s\in H\).  A truncated-factorization step preserves it by the finite chain rule.  A fixing step records the actual current conditional \(m\), forms \(K'=K/m\), and records the reversible identity
\[
 mK'=K.
\tag{2}
\]
The Algorithm--2 hybrid step and the final district product and marginalization preserve the represented kernel by the local identities proved in \(\textnormal{thm:transition-soundness-termination}\).  Finally, a residual projection is accepted only when, componentwise, its generated numerator \(P\), denominator product \(D\), and the retained constraint polynomials \(J_1,\ldots,J_M\) satisfy an exact polynomial identity
\[
 D(\xi)t_{a,H}^N(\xi)-P\{o_H^N(\xi)\}
 =\sum_{j=1}^M h_j(\xi)J_j(\xi).
\tag{3}
\]
For \(\eta\in\mathcal I_H\), every \(J_j(\eta)=0\) by the intrinsic definition of \(\mathcal I_H\).  Thus the same invariant holds whether the formula was assembled by the nonresidual cases or accepted by the residual projection verifier.

By \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\), every actual context, chain-rule, fixing, or elimination divisor recorded on this branch is positive at \(O_H^N(\eta)=O_H(\theta)\), and every branch-required supported cell is positive.  Hence
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\tag{4}
\]
All cross-multiplications in the transition induction, including (2) and (3), are therefore reversible on the compatible image.  At the terminal label the represented normalized kernel is \(t_{a,H}^N\), so (1) and (4) give
\[
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}
 =F_H\{O_H^N(\eta)\}
 =T_{a,H}^N(\eta)
 =T_{a,H}(\theta),
 \qquad \theta\in\Theta_H.
\tag{5}
\]
Because \(F_H\) is defined only on \(\mathfrak D_H\), equation (5) asserts nothing at an ambient table outside that branch domain.

Suppose next that \(\kappa_H\) is negative, and fix \(b\in\mathcal B_H\).  Let \(\eta_b^+\) and \(\eta_b^-\) be the two rational-affine normalized records generated before gate reinsertion.  The verifier checks, for each sign, all primitive simplex inequalities and all equalities \(g_H=0\), as well as
\[
 s_H^N(\eta_b^\pm)(s)>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s\in H
\tag{6}
\]
and
\[
 o_H^N(\eta_b^\pm)(c)>0
 \quad\text{for every }c\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+).
\tag{7}
\]
These are precisely the intrinsic membership conditions for \(\mathcal I_H\), including the retained root-factorization and gate-sharing equations.  Therefore \(\eta_b^\pm\in\mathcal I_H\), and the well-typed reinsertion maps give
\[
 \theta_b^\pm:=\rho_H(\eta_b^\pm)\in\Theta_H.
\tag{8}
\]
The other two acceptance tests are equality of every supported observation polynomial and a target-difference polynomial having a certified nonzero constant sign throughout the open rational box.  Consequently
\[
 O_H^N(\eta_b^+)=O_H^N(\eta_b^-),
 \qquad
 T_{a,H}^N(\eta_b^+)\ne T_{a,H}^N(\eta_b^-).
\tag{9}
\]
Applying the mutual-inverse identities of \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\) to (8)--(9) yields
\[
 O_H(\theta_b^+)=O_H(\theta_b^-),
 \qquad
 T_{a,H}(\theta_b^+)\ne T_{a,H}(\theta_b^-).
\tag{10}
\]
Membership in \(\Theta_H\), together with (6)--(7), also gives selector support exactly \(H\) and strict positivity on every structurally admissible supported cell.  Equations (4)--(5) and (8)--(10) prove the two asserted certificate alternatives.

Fix a positive certificate, \(\theta\in\Theta_H\), and \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\), and suppose that \(\mathbf p_H\) lies in the differentiable interior of the branch domain \(\mathfrak D_H\).  Put \(C=\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\).  The declared finite categorical model makes \(m_H=|C|<\infty\).  For \(X_i=(V_i,S_i)\), the empirical vector satisfies
\[
 \widehat{\mathbf p}_H=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n e_{X_i}^C,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{p_H}(e_{X_i}^C)=\mathbf p_H.
\tag{1}
\]
The branch domain is given by finitely many strict coordinate and registered-denominator inequalities.  Those defining functions are continuous.  Interiority therefore gives a relative neighborhood \(N\) of \(\mathbf p_H\) in the simplex and \(\delta>0\) such that the relative \(\ell_\infty\)-ball of radius \(\delta\) is contained in \(N\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\).  Since
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H(c)\}
 =\frac{p_H(c)\{1-p_H(c)\}}{n},
\]
Chebyshev's inequality in each of the finitely many coordinates and a union bound imply
\[
 \Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat{\mathbf p}_H\notin N\}
 \le
 \frac1{n\delta^2}\sum_{c\in C}p_H(c)\{1-p_H(c)\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{2}
\]
In particular, \(\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\notin\mathfrak D_H\}\to0\).

All registered denominators remain nonzero on a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(\mathbf p_H\).  The finite rational circuit \(F_H\) thus has a continuously differentiable ambient-coordinate extension there.  Taylor expansion, (1), and the fact that
\[
 \mathbb E_{p_H}\left\|\sqrt n
 (\widehat{\mathbf p}_H-\mathbf p_H)\right\|_2^2
 =\operatorname{tr}\{\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf p_H)
 -\mathbf p_H\mathbf p_H^{\mathsf T}\}<\infty
\]
give, on the on-domain event,
\[
 F_H(\widehat p_H)-F_H(p_H)
 =J_H(\mathbf p_H)(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H-\mathbf p_H)
 +o_p(n^{-1/2})
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{IF}_H(X_i)+o_p(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{3}
\]
The influence function in (3) has mean zero by (1) and finite variance because \(C\) is finite.  The same differentiability calculation along every local multinomial submodel establishes regularity.  Thus \(\textnormal{lem:asymptotic-linear-normality}\), after premultiplication by any fixed \(c\in\mathbb R^{k_Y}\), gives
\[
 \sqrt n\,c^{\mathsf T}
 \{F_H(\widehat p_H)-F_H(p_H)\}
 \rightsquigarrow
 N\bigl(0,c^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Hc\bigr).
\tag{4}
\]

On the reporting event, expansion of the defined empirical influence functions gives the exact identity
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_H
 =J_H(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)
 \{\operatorname{diag}(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)
 -\widehat{\mathbf p}_H\widehat{\mathbf p}_H^{\mathsf T}\}
 J_H(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{5}
\]
Equation (2) gives \(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H\to\mathbf p_H\) in probability, and the Jacobian of a rational circuit is continuous wherever its registered denominators are nonzero.  Hence
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_H\longrightarrow
 J_H(\mathbf p_H)
 \{\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf p_H)-\mathbf p_H\mathbf p_H^{\mathsf T}\}
 J_H(\mathbf p_H)^{\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma_H
 \quad\text{in probability},
\tag{6}
\]
where the last equality is the variance of the influence function in (3).

By \(\textnormal{thm:certificate-soundness}\), \(F_H(p_H)=Q_{a,H}\).  For fixed \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), take \(c=e_y^Y\) in (4).  If
\[
 v_{H,y}:=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H e_y^Y>0,
\]
then (6) gives \(\widehat v_{H,y}/v_{H,y}\to1\) in probability and \(\Pr(\widehat v_{H,y}>0)\to1\).  Therefore
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat Q_{a,H}(y)-Q_{a,H}(y)\}}
 {\sqrt{\widehat v_{H,y}}}
 \rightsquigarrow N(0,1).
\tag{7}
\]
The definition of \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\), equations (2) and (7), and the fact that no interval is reported off the domain imply
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,
 Q_{a,H}(y)\in CI_y\}=1-\alpha.
\tag{8}
\]

For a fixed nonzero \(\lambda\) with \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H\lambda>0\), take \(c=\lambda\) in (4) and premultiply (6) by \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\lambda\).  The same studentization argument yields
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,
 \lambda^{\mathsf T}Q_{a,H}\in CI_{\lambda}\}=1-\alpha.
\tag{9}
\]
The neighborhoods used in (2) depend on the fixed interior law.  Thus (8)--(9) are pointwise statements and make no uniform claim as a supported cell or registered denominator approaches zero; on the off-domain event the output is \(\bot_H\), not an estimate.

Fix \(\theta\in\Theta_H\) and write \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\).  Order the entries of the accepting branch ledger by creation time.  We prove simultaneously, by induction over this order, that every recorded divisor is positive and that every current-kernel cell marked branch-reachable by the ledger is positive.

For a selected context \(s\in H\), the base divisor is
\[
 d_s=p_H(S=s)=
 \sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v,s).
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\textnormal{ass:exact-selector-support}\), \(d_s>0\), so the displayed summation set is nonempty.  Each structurally admissible summand is positive by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\).  Hence the initialized context cells \(p_H(v,s)/d_s\) are positive.  Evaluating a known selector gate changes no probability by division and therefore preserves this base claim.

Assume the simultaneous claim through ledger entry \(j-1\).  A denominator introduced by \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}\) is, by \(\textnormal{def:kernel-operations}\), the actual marginal of the current positive kernel over a nonempty branch-reachable conditioning fiber.  It therefore has the form
\[
 d_j=\sum_{x\in B_j}K_j(x)>0,
 \qquad B_j\ne\varnothing,
\tag{2}
\]
because every summand is positive by the induction hypothesis.  The resulting conditional is a ratio of positive quantities and its reachable cells remain positive.

At a computed fixing step, the divisor is the actual current nested conditional, constructed from current-kernel marginals.  Its numerator and conditioning marginal are nonempty sums of positive reachable cells, so both are positive by the preceding paragraph; the conditional is therefore positive.  The successor identity is recorded as
\[
 d_jK_{j+1}=K_j.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus every reachable successor cell is positive.  The same conclusion holds for a hybrid product because it is a finite product of positive truncated conditional factors, and ancestor marginalization preserves positivity by a nonempty finite sum.

Finally, a residual-elimination divisor is eligible only after cancellation and sign normalization have produced the exact ledger factorization
\[
 d_j(p_H)=r_j
 \prod_{i\in E_j}d_i(p_H)
 \prod_{\ell=1}^{L_j}
 \left\{\sum_{x\in B_{j\ell}}K_{j\ell}(p_H,x)\right\},
 \qquad r_j\in\mathbb Q_{>0},
\tag{4}
\]
where \(E_j\subseteq\{1,\ldots,j-1\}\), every \(B_{j\ell}\) is nonempty, and every displayed kernel cell is marked branch-reachable.  The first product in (4) is positive by induction, and every sum in the second product is positive by the simultaneous kernel-cell claim.  Hence \(d_j(p_H)>0\).

Finite induction proves positivity of every actual divisor retained in \(\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}}\), including any intermediate divisor later cancelled from the reduced terminal expression.  The branch-required coordinate inequalities also hold by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\).  Therefore \(p_H\in\mathfrak D_H\).  Since \(\theta\) was arbitrary,
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\]
All inequalities are pointwise at the chosen compatible law; no common positive lower bound has been used.

Define
\[
 \mathcal R_H=
 \left\{\theta\in\Theta(G^+):
 \operatorname{supp}_{p_\theta}(S)=H,\quad
 p_\theta(c)>0\ \text{for every }c\in
 \mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The probabilities in (1) are well typed because \(\textnormal{ass:finite-categorical}\) gives finite alphabets and the recursive SCM semantics defines \(p_\theta\).  By the definition of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)\), that class imposes the common recursive selector-gated syntax, independent-root factorization, and canonical response representation before the two restrictions in (1).  By \(\textnormal{def:model-class}\), \(\Theta_H\) imposes exactly that common syntax together with those restrictions.  Therefore
\[
 \Theta_H=\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)\cap\mathcal R_H
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+).
\tag{2}
\]
If the published class contains a parameter violating either restriction in (1), it belongs to the right-hand class in (2) but not to \(\Theta_H\), which proves the asserted conditional strictness.

By the declared support-exact global-twin relation,
\[
 \mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}
 =\{(\theta^+,\theta^-)\in\Theta_H^2:
 O_H(\theta^+)=O_H(\theta^-),\ 
 T_{a,H}(\theta^+)\ne T_{a,H}(\theta^-)\}.
\tag{3}
\]
Taking Cartesian squares in (2) and using (3) gives
\[
 \mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}
 \subseteq\Theta_H^2
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)^2.
\tag{4}
\]
Moreover, \(\textnormal{thm:certificate-soundness}\) implies that every verifier-accepted negative certificate lies in the set on the right side of (3); an unverified failure tag does not.

Now let \(w=(\theta^+,\theta^-)\in\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\).  If either coordinate assigns positive selector mass to some \(s_0\notin H\), then that coordinate is outside \(\Theta_H\) by \(\textnormal{ass:exact-selector-support}\), so (3) excludes \(w\).  If instead some \(c_0\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\) has \(p_{\theta^\varepsilon}(c_0)=0\) for \(\varepsilon\in\{+,-\}\), then \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\) again puts that coordinate outside \(\Theta_H\).  Finally, if equality fails on any coordinate of \(O_H\), the equality required in (3) fails directly.  Each listed defect therefore implies
\[
 w\notin\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}.
\tag{5}
\]
The definition of \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\) does not itself impose any of these three additional fixed-support obligations.  Hence membership in the published failure relation alone does not imply membership in \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).  If the published relation contains a pair with one of the defects, (5) supplies an element of
\(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\setminus\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\), proving the final noninclusion.

Fix a successful execution of Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser Algorithms 1--2 that uses only selector values in \(H\) and only denominators supported on \(\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\).  By \(\textnormal{lem:lgs-case-refinement}\), each existential published case is represented by a finite decidable candidate set in the input-determined machine.  Whenever the published predicate has a witness, canonical enumeration has a least passing witness, so the machine cannot take the corresponding exhaustion failure.  Thus it reaches a formula result and never selects a context outside \(H\).

The same refinement lemma shows, inductively over the published recursion, that the machine's canonically selected context, computed valid fixing sequence, and Algorithm--2 triple return the same district kernel as the published step on \(O_H^N(\mathcal I_H)\).  This conclusion uses fixing-order invariance only after both sequences have been proved valid and uses the hybrid-kernel identity only after the displayed conditional-independence and reachability predicates pass.  District multiplication and ancestor marginalization therefore make the terminal machine circuit extensionally equal to the successful published circuit on the normalized compatible image.

Every division actually made by the machine is entered in its own step-indexed ledger.  By \(\textnormal{lem:step-indexed-ledger-positivity}\),
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\tag{1}
\]
Because a successful published output identifies the normalized causal query, the extensional equality just proved gives, for \(\eta=\nu_H(\theta)\),
\[
 F_H\{O_H^N(\eta)\}=T_{a,H}^N(\eta).
\tag{2}
\]
Normalization equivalence supplies
\[
 O_H^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}=O_H(\theta),
 \qquad
 T_{a,H}^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta).
\tag{3}
\]
Substituting (3) into (2) yields
\[
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta),
 \qquad \theta\in\Theta_H.
\tag{4}
\]
Reinserting stored gate syntax reverses the normalized context substitutions, so the machine circuit and every support-licensed published output agree at every point of \(O_H(\Theta_H)\).  Equation (1) certifies the machine's actual divisors.  Distinct successful presentations may use different contexts, normalizers, or ledgers; the argument requires no equality among those presentations and introduces no selector value outside \(H\).

Unique initialization and a total deterministic successor are given by \(\textnormal{prop:input-determinacy}\).  From any reachable running state with a nonresidual task, \(\textnormal{lem:nonresidual-progress}\) supplies a unique successor and excludes a stuck nonresidual control state.

We first verify local soundness.  A selected context and its normalized kernel equal evaluation of the known selector gates by \(\textnormal{lem:context-construction-soundness}\).  The operator \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}\) is the finite chain-rule factorization, with its actual conditioning marginals, by \(\textnormal{lem:truncated-factorization-identity}\).  Once a valid sequence has been computed, every fixing quotient and its graph update preserve the represented kernel relation by \(\textnormal{lem:computed-fixing-soundness}\).  A passing Algorithm--2 triple yields the required district kernel by \(\textnormal{lem:hybrid-kernel-soundness}\), and sound district factors assemble to the target by \(\textnormal{lem:district-assembly-soundness}\).  By \(\textnormal{lem:step-indexed-ledger-positivity}\), every divisor in these identities is positive on the compatible image, so each recorded cross-multiplication is reversible there.

For a residual projection, the verifier requires the exact componentwise identity
\[
 D\,t_{a,H}^N-P(o_H^N)=0
\tag{1}
\]
modulo the retained constraints and requires every divisor in \(D\) to occur in the positive ledger.  Evaluation of (1) on \(\mathcal I_H\) and division by \(D>0\) proves the emitted formula identity.  For a residual contrast, the verifier checks primitive-simplex membership, the retained equalities, exact selector-support signs, strict supported-cell signs, equality of every observation polynomial, and a target contrast of nonzero constant sign.  Gate reinsertion is valid by \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\), so the emitted pair is a genuine global twin.  Exhausting the finite generated list emits only \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}\), never a causal conclusion.  This proves local soundness for every possible transition.

It remains to prove termination.  Lexicographic order on \(\mathbb N^4\) is well founded: an infinite descending sequence would force the first coordinate eventually to stabilize, then the second, third, and fourth, contradicting strict descent.  More explicitly, map a task rank \((n,c,f,k)\) to
\[
 \rho(n,c,f,k)=\omega^3n+\omega^2c+\omega f+k<\omega^4.
\tag{2}
\]
For a finite work multiset \(M\), let
\[
 \Omega(M)=\mathop{\#\!\sum}_{\tau\in M}
 \omega^{\rho\{r_I(\tau)\}},
\tag{3}
\]
where \(\#\!\sum\) denotes finite natural sum.  If one task is removed or is replaced by finitely many tasks of strictly smaller rank, the coefficient of the largest affected exponent in the Cantor normal form of (3) decreases and all new terms have smaller exponents.  Hence \(\Omega\) strictly decreases.  Since ordinals are well ordered, (3) directly proves well-foundedness of the finite-multiset extension used for \(\mu_H\).

Now inspect the exhaustive cases in \(\operatorname{next}_I\).  A Start task and a district split replace one task by finitely many proper-ambient children, or by equal-ambient administrative children at lower control levels.  Ancestor restriction lowers the ambient size unless it is merely an administrative phase change, in which case the control level decreases.  Each fixing step lowers the remaining-fix coordinate, and its last step invokes a lower-control continuation.  Each rejected Algorithm--2 candidate lowers the remaining-candidate coordinate; a passing candidate enters lower-control hybrid fixing.  Factor storage and Join completion remove tasks.  Thus every nonterminal nonresidual successor strictly decreases \(\mu_H\).  The residual generator is finite; testing a rejected residual candidate lowers its finite remaining-candidate coordinate, while acceptance or exhaustion terminates that task.  Therefore an infinite run is impossible.

The finite run cannot end at a running nonresidual state by nonresidual progress.  Its only endpoints are a formula, one verifier-accepted global twin, or one \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}\) result.  Determinacy makes the endpoint unique.  This proves local soundness, finite termination, and the assertion that a pending residual is the sole noncertificate endpoint.

We first reduce the graphical cases from the displayed binary input.  In the target LS-SWIG, \(A\) and \(S\) are fixed, while \(W_0\) and \(Z_0\) have no children.  Hence the random ancestor set of \(Y\) is
\[
 Y^*=\{Y\},
\]
and its only district is \(D^*=\{Y\}\).  In the observed latent projection, the shared root \(U_0\) gives \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), the shared root \(R_0\) gives \(S\leftrightarrow Y\), and the selector gate gives \(S\to A\), while \(A\to Y\).  Neither \(S\) nor \(A\) is initially fixable while the other and \(Y\) remain: its district-descendant intersection contains a proper descendant.  Consequently no proper reachable superset of \(\{Y\}\) is obtained by fixing a complement, whereas \(\{S,A,Y\}\) is trivially reachable.  By \(\textnormal{lem:computed-closure-valid-sequence}\), the computed closure is therefore
\[
 C=\{S,A,Y\}\supsetneq D^*.
\tag{1}
\]
Since \(S\in C\), the deterministic machine enters Algorithm 2.

Here \(\operatorname{ch}^*(S)=\{A\}\).  At \(s=0\) the serious set is empty, so that value supplies no triple; at \(\bar s=1\), the known gate forces \(A=1\), and \(Z=\{A\}\) is the unique nonempty serious choice.  Districts in the mechanically constructed LS-SWIG partition its vertices, so there is at most one district \(D'\) containing \(D^*\).  For the computed candidate, the edge induced by the shared root \(R_0\) leaves \(S\) adjacent by a bidirected edge to \(Y(\bar s)\).  The line-7 conditioning set contains neither endpoint in a way that blocks this length-one path.  Thus the required d-separation fails.  There are no further supported nonempty-serious triples, so canonical enumeration exhausts and returns
\[
 \operatorname{LGSFailA2NoCandidate}(D^*,C),
\tag{2}
\]
after which it creates the tagged residual task.  This reduction uses only the input graph and the current state, consistently with \(\textnormal{prop:input-determinacy}\).

We next verify the generated residual contrast.  Index the four \(A=1\) response rows by \((u_0,r_0)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), and put
\[
 r=(3/4,1/4,1/4,3/4),
 \qquad d=(-4,-1,0,3).
\tag{3}
\]
Only two observation rows can change: the \(Y=1\) cells with \(A=1\) in the natural and forced contexts.  After multiplying these two coefficient rows by their positive common denominators, the generator's observation matrix is
\[
 M=\begin{pmatrix}2&1&6&3\\1&2&1&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its deterministic rational row reduction is
\[
 \operatorname{rref}(M)=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&0&11/3&4/3\\0&1&-4/3&1/3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Setting the third free coordinate to zero and the fourth to three produces the primitive integer null vector \((-4,-1,0,3)\), and direct multiplication gives \(Md^{\mathsf T}=0\).  Thus the fixed free-column enumeration produces \(d\) from the residual payload rather than receiving it as a desired target contrast.

For a binary response subtable \(f\in\{0,1\}^4\), define
\[
 \pi_0(f)=\prod_{j=1}^4r_j^{f(j)}(1-r_j)^{1-f(j)},
\]
\[
 \delta(f)=\pi_0(f)\sum_{j=1}^4
 \frac{d_j\{f(j)-r_j\}}{r_j(1-r_j)},
 \qquad
 \pi_b(f)=\pi_0(f)+b\delta(f).
\tag{4}
\]
Keep the \(A=0\) response rows at their baseline law and combine them with (4); this defines a law on full canonical response tables.  Independence of the four Bernoulli coordinates under \(\pi_0\) gives
\[
 \sum_f\delta(f)=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_f\pi_b(f)f(j)=r_j+bd_j.
\tag{5}
\]
The smallest possible value of the score multiplying \(b\) in (4) is
\[
 -\frac{16}{3}-4-12=-\frac{64}{3}.
\]
Therefore \(0<b<1/32\) implies \(\pi_b(f)>\pi_0(f)/3>0\) for every table.  Thus (4) is a rational-affine path inside the full canonical response simplex, as required by \(\textnormal{ass:canonical-response-richness}\).

From \(S=R_0\mathbin\oplus N_S\),
\[
 P(S=0\mid R_0=0)=\frac23,
 \qquad
 P(S=0\mid R_0=1)=\frac13,
\tag{6}
\]
with the probabilities reversed for \(S=1\).  At \(S=0\),
\[
 P(A=1\mid U_0=0)=\frac14,
 \qquad
 P(A=1\mid U_0=1)=\frac34.
\tag{7}
\]
Using (3), the coefficient of \(b\) in the natural-context cell \(P(S=0,A=1,Y=1)\) is
\[
 \frac14\frac23\left\{\frac14(-4)+\frac34(0)\right\}
 +\frac14\frac13\left\{\frac14(-1)+\frac34(3)\right\}=0.
\tag{8}
\]
In the forced context \(S=1,A=1\), the coefficient is
\[
 \frac14\frac13(-4+0)+\frac14\frac23(-1+3)=0.
\tag{9}
\]
No \(A=0\) response row is perturbed, and equality of each \(Y=0\) cell follows from its unchanged \((S,A)\) margin and equality of the corresponding \(Y=1\) cell.  Direct evaluation at \(b=0\) yields, in the stated cell order,
\[
 (13,11,13,11,24,24)/96.
\tag{10}
\]
Equations (8)--(9) prove that (10) is constant throughout the box.  Its smallest entry is \(11/96>0\).  Appending the independent fair variables \(W_0,Z_0\) multiplies every full observed cell by \(1/4\), so the complete observed laws agree and remain strictly positive.  Equation (6) and the fair law of \(R_0\) give \(P(S=0)=P(S=1)=1/2\), hence selector support is exactly \(H=\{0,1\}\).

Under \(do(A=1,S=s_{\emptyset})\), the independent pair \((U_0,R_0)\) remains uniform.  By (3) and (5),
\[
 T_b(Y=1)=\frac12+b\frac{-4-1+0+3}{4}
 =\frac12-\frac b2.
\tag{11}
\]
The simplex inequalities following (4), the observation identities (8)--(10), exact support, strict cell positivity, and the constant-sign contrast (11) are exactly the residual verifier's acceptance conditions.  Hence it accepts the pair consisting of the model at \(b=0\) and the model at \(b\) for every \(0<b<1/32\).  At \(b=1/64\), (11) equals \(63/128\), whereas the baseline target is \(1/2\), completing the certificate computation.

proposed.statement: Every returned certificate \(\kappa_H\) is sound over \(\Theta_H\). On a formula branch, the registry contains every context normalizer, reachable fixing margin, and reduced rational-elimination denominator together with its positivity-ledger factorization; \(O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\), and \(F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\). No value is asserted outside \(\mathfrak D_H\). On a negative branch, for every \(b\in\mathcal B_H\), \(\theta_b^{+},\theta_b^{-}\in\Theta_H\), \(O_H(\theta_b^{+})=O_H(\theta_b^{-})\), and \(T_{a,H}(\theta_b^{+})\ne T_{a,H}(\theta_b^{-})\); both laws have selector support exactly \(H\) and strictly positive structurally admissible cells.

proposed.gap: The 2024 anchor proves witnesses for specified failures but does not furnish a fixed-support global pair on every residual branch or an open family of legal pairs.
proposed.consumer: A provenance-aware do-search backend can return machine-checkable formulas or verified legal twins, and can distinguish them from pending residual diagnostics.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and a positive certificate. Use \(\operatorname{vec}_H=(\iota_C,\iota_Y)\), the \(k_Y\times m_H\) Jacobian \(J_H\), \(\operatorname{IF}_H(c)=J_H(\mathbf p_H)(e_c^C-\mathbf p_H)\), and \(\Sigma_H=\operatorname{Var}_{p_H}\{\operatorname{IF}_H(V,S)\}\). At every fixed \(p_H\) in the differentiable interior of its branch-specific \(\mathfrak D_H\), \(\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\notin\mathfrak D_H\}\to0\), and \(F_H(\widehat p_H)\) is asymptotically linear on the on-domain event. For fixed \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), set \(\widehat Q_{a,H}(y)=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}F_H(\widehat p_H)\), \(\widehat v_{H,y}=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}\widehat\Sigma_H e_y^Y\), and \(CI_y=[\widehat Q_{a,H}(y)\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat v_{H,y}/n}]\). If \(\Sigma_H\{\iota_Y(y),\iota_Y(y)\}>0\), then
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,\ Q_{a,H}(y)\in CI_y\}=1-\alpha.
\]
For fixed nonzero \(\lambda\) with \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H\lambda>0\), use the defined \(CI_{\lambda}\); then
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,\ \lambda^{\mathsf T}Q_{a,H}\in CI_{\lambda}\}=1-\alpha.
\]
Thus the coverage targets are respectively the single component \(Q_{a,H}(y)\) and the fixed scalar contrast \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}Q_{a,H}\), each pointwise at the fixed interior law. On the off-domain event the procedure returns \(\bot_H\) and no confidence set; no positivity-boundary-uniform coverage is claimed.
proposed.justification: The statistical rung turns every positive graphical certificate into an estimable finite-table causal functional.
proposed.gap: Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser derive inference for fixing functionals, but not for one joint fixed-support selector table generated by the proposed calculus.
proposed.consumer: Applied users of a selector-aware do-search backend obtain point estimates, standard errors, and pointwise Wald intervals from the same returned circuit.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The finite-dimensional empirical-table argument directly uses the finite-categorical assumption, so the dependency is made explicit without changing the claim.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the converse for every generated ResidualPending state: a fiber-constant target must have a verifier-encoded rational projection, while a nonconstant target must have a rational-affine support-exact global-twin box.
open_obligations.obstruction: The deterministic task machine reaches residuals without circular scheduling, but finiteness of the candidate generators does not imply their exhaustiveness. The frozen primitives neither exclude an identified residual with only a nonrational algebraic observable representative nor prove that a common signed response-row contrast lifts through every interacting district and observed descendant while preserving exact selector support.
open_obligations.attempted: Reused the established input determinacy, computed closure and fixing, local context, truncated-factorization, hybrid and Join identities, denominator induction, multiset termination, successful LGS refinement, binary residual certificate, and ordinary-ID specialization. Proved the sound formula and twin implications without inserting a successful trace, an extensional identification oracle, or unrestricted quantifier elimination into the machine.
open_obligations.partial_result: The input-determined redesign proves unique initialization and scheduling, every nonresidual local identity, step-indexed denominator positivity, finite-multiset termination, preservation of each successful support-licensed Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser branch, the binary residual certificate, and the ordinary-ID structural specialization.  Certificate soundness gives both one-way implications: a returned formula is constant on each \(O_H\)-fiber, while a returned support-exact global-twin box proves nonidentification.  The sole missing implication is \(\textnormal{oeq:all-residual-dichotomy}\): for every \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}\) payload, prove either a verifier-accepted rational projection or a verifier-accepted support-exact common response contrast, including exclusion of a fiber-constant target whose observable representative is only nonrational algebraic.

prose_updates.tldr: For finite selector-gated semi-Markovian SCMs observed on exactly \(H\), retained support normalization and a deterministic Algorithms 1--2 task machine preserve every successful support-licensed formula, certify every actual division, and terminate at a sound formula, a verifier-accepted support-exact twin, or an explicitly pending residual. The all-residual rational-formula-or-global-twin dichotomy remains the sole missing step, so the field completeness headline is preserved but is not claimed as proved.

project_justification.gap: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser give a sound systematic-selection recursion and witnesses for specified failures, but not an input-determined fixed-support execution semantics or an all-residual exact-support converse. The redesigned machine closes the execution gap without importing a successful trace; residual candidate exhaustiveness alone remains open.
project_justification.niche: The setting fixes one coherent joint selector law on exactly \(H\). Supported contexts share natural mechanisms and selector provenance, while absent contexts cannot be invoked. This differs from ordinary observational ID and from data-fusion formulations that supply separate experiments.
project_justification.fill: The proved layer supplies intrinsic support normalization, canonical finite graph computations, explicit recursive work tasks, computed valid fixing sequences, distinct truncated factorization and fixing, a step-indexed positivity ledger, multiset termination, positive-branch preservation, sound formula and twin verification, pointwise interior inference, and an ordinary-ID structural specialization. The intended field result additionally requires the open all-residual rational-projection-or-global-contrast theorem.

sampling_model.overlap: Every structurally admissible supported cell is strictly positive. Each context normalizer, chain-rule conditioning marginal, actual nested-fixing conditional, and accepted elimination divisor used by a returned formula is recorded in a step-indexed ledger and proved positive by induction. No common numerical lower bound and no positivity outside \(H\) are imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On a formula branch, estimate the finite table \(p_H\) empirically and evaluate the returned rational circuit only on its ledger-projected domain \(\mathfrak D_H\). Pointwise Wald inference is valid at each fixed differentiable interior law with positive target variance. A pending residual is an algorithmic certificate gap, not a point estimate or a nonidentification conclusion.

prose_updates.related_work: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser (2024) provide the selector-gated model and Algorithms 1--2. The present positive result is a line-by-line, input-determined refinement: every graph, context, closure, fixing sequence, hybrid factor, and denominator is computed from the finite input and current state, and every successful support-licensed branch is preserved. Shpitser and Pearl (2006) provide the ordinary ID formula-or-hedge endpoint; the new machine specializes structurally to that recursion when the selector is constant and separated. Tabell, Tikka, and Karvanen (2026) give pruning and clustering for general data fusion but no fixed-support parameter-image converse. The remaining novelty claim is confined to exact-support residual exhaustion, which is still open.
prose_updates.interpretation: A positive output is an explicit rational map of the supplied joint selector table, together with every denominator needed to evaluate it. A verifier-accepted negative output is an open rational family of canonical SCM pairs sharing the entire admissible observed law and exact selector support while disagreeing on the intervention target. An LGS failure tag or ResidualPending output carries neither conclusion by itself.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Nonresidual circularity is removed: initialization, closure, contexts, conditional-independence tests, fixing orders, hybrid products, spawned district work, and denominator proofs are finite deterministic computations. The unresolved issue is semantic rather than operational: it is unknown whether every generated residual has a rational identifying projection or a common rational-affine response contrast preserving all supported observed descendants. Boundary-uniform inference and unrestricted quantifier elimination remain outside scope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Proved here are support normalization, input determinacy, computed closure and fixing, local context and kernel identities, step-indexed denominator positivity, no-stuck nonresidual progress, multiset termination, preservation of successful published positive formulas, certificate soundness, the binary Algorithm-2 residual certificate, pointwise interior Wald inference, and ordinary-ID structural reduction. The formula-or-global-twin completeness theorem remains open exactly through \(\textnormal{oeq:all-residual-dichotomy}\); no LGS failure tag is promoted to nonidentification without a verified global twin, and no absent selector context is supplied.

proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\bar G\) denote the graph obtained from \(G_H^N\) by suppressing the selector coordinate and its stored gate syntax, and let \(\bar\Theta^{+}\) be the canonical response-function model class on \(\bar G\) with the admissible-cell interior inherited from \(\Theta_H\).  We first identify this suppressed model and then compare the two recursions.

Because \(H=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), exact selector support gives
\[
 p_\theta(S=s_{\emptyset})=1
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 p_\theta(S=s)=0\quad(s\ne s_{\emptyset}).                                      \tag{1}
\]
Every selector-controlled \(X\in V\) has, by the known-multiplexer assumption, an equation of the form
\[
 X=\begin{cases}
 f_X^{\mathrm{nat}}(\operatorname{pa}_X,U_X),&S_X^e=0,\\
 S_X^v,&S_X^e=1.
 \end{cases}                                                                       \tag{2}
\]
The laid-back hypothesis says that \(s_{\emptyset,X}^e=0\) for every such \(X\).  Substitution of (1) into (2) therefore yields
\[
 X=f_X^{\mathrm{nat}}(\operatorname{pa}_X,U_X)                                    \tag{3}
\]
at the sole observed execution and at the target execution.  Thus no selector-specified intervention value is an argument of a substantive equation after normalization.  By the definition of \(N_H\), an argument is deleted only when unused on every element of
\(E_H=H\cup\{s_{\emptyset}\}=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), while all primitive natural-response coordinates are retained.  Consequently the substantive equations and their canonical response tables in \(G_H^N\), after suppression of the constant selector, are exactly those of the ordinary recursive semi-Markovian expansion \(\bar G\) on \(V\).

The assumption that \(S\) has no latent root shared with \(V\), together with the declared independent-root factorization, implies that marginalizing the selector roots leaves precisely the declared semi-Markovian root law for the substantive equations (3).  Hence restriction of \(\theta\in\Theta_H\) to the substantive response coordinates defines a parameter \(R(\theta)\in\bar\Theta^{+}\).  Conversely, any \(\bar\theta\in\bar\Theta^{+}\) extends to an element \(E(\bar\theta)\in\Theta_H\) by adjoining the point mass at \(s_{\emptyset}\), the prescribed multiplexers, and arbitrary retained selector-only coordinates satisfying their simplex constraints.  This extension has exact support \(H\); its admissible cells are positive because those cells are precisely \((v,s_{\emptyset})\) with \(\bar p_{\bar\theta}(v)>0\).  Recursive evaluation of (3) gives, for every \(v\) and \(y\),
\[
 p_\theta(V=v,S=s_{\emptyset})=p_{R(\theta)}^{\bar G}(V=v),
 \qquad
 T_{a,H}(\theta)(y)
 =p_{R(\theta)}^{\bar G}\{Y(a)=y\},                                                \tag{4}
\]
and the same equalities with \(\theta=E(\bar\theta)\).  It follows in both directions that, under the canonical identification
\(q(v,s_{\emptyset})\leftrightarrow q(v)\),
\[
 \Phi_H
 =\left\{\left(p_{\bar\theta}^{\bar G}(V),
 p_{\bar\theta}^{\bar G}\{Y(a)\}\right):
 \bar\theta\in\bar\Theta^{+}\right\}.                                           \tag{5}
\]
The normalization-equivalence theorem identifies the left side of (5) equally with the normalized attainable relation.  This proves the first two assertions, including that retained dormant syntax does not enlarge or shrink the observed--target relation.

It remains to compare the case function with ordinary ID.  Let \(\bar I\) be the ordinary input consisting of \(\bar G\), \(A\), \(a\), \(Y\), and the law \(\bar p(v)=p_H(v,s_{\emptyset})\).  We couple the support-aware and ordinary recursions by the invariant
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\text{the current substantive CADMGs are equal after suppression of }S,\\
 &q(x_V,S=s_{\emptyset})=\bar q(x_V),\\
 &\text{the pending outcome set, districts, fixed sets, and stored factors agree.}
 \end{aligned}                                                                     \tag{6}
\]
At initialization, (6) follows from (4) and from the definition of
\(\operatorname{init}_H\).  The Start transition constructs the same intervention graph, the same ancestor set
\[
 Y^*=\operatorname{an}_{\bar G(a)}(Y),                                               \tag{7}
\]
and the same canonically ordered districts, because the constant separated selector has no substantive arrow or bidirected connection after (3).

For every pending substantive district \(D^*\), laid-backness and the absence of a selector-forced treatment coordinate imply
\[
 L(D^*)=\{s_{\emptyset}\}.                                                         \tag{8}
\]
Thus the positive-context failure case is impossible.  Moreover, for every substantive vertex \(W\) and every successively fixed substantive CADMG, suppression of the separated selector preserves both districts and descendants of \(W\).  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{dis}_{G}(W)\cap\operatorname{de}_{G}(W)=\{W\}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{dis}_{\bar G}(W)\cap\operatorname{de}_{\bar G}(W)=\{W\}.           \tag{9}
\]
Equation (9), induction along a proposed sequence, and the definition of
\(\operatorname{valid}\) show that the same substantive sequences are valid in the two computations.  Since both use the same restricted canonical order, \(\operatorname{fixSeq}\) returns the same least sequence.  The proved computed-closure lemma then implies that the selected reachable closure of \(D^*\) is the ordinary reachable closure \(C\subseteq V\).  In particular,
\[
 S\notin C.                                                                         \tag{10}
\]

If \(C=D^*\), the case function fixes the computed complement and evaluates at the sole context.  Under (6), every current-kernel marginal used in a fixing conditional is the corresponding ordinary marginal.  Its denominator is positive by the inherited interior condition, so each division is defined, and direct cancellation gives
\[
 \left.
 \phi_{V\setminus D^*}(p_H;G_H^{[]})
 \right|_{S=s_{\emptyset}}
 =\phi_{V\setminus D^*}(\bar p;\bar G).                                             \tag{11}
\]
Thus the emitted district factor is the ordinary reachable factor and (6) is preserved.

If \(C\ne D^*\), the computed valid sequence for \(V\setminus C\) similarly gives
\[
 \left.\widetilde q\right|_{S=s_{\emptyset}}
 =\phi_{V\setminus C}(\bar p;\bar G),
 \qquad
 \widetilde G[s_{\emptyset}]=\bar G_C.                                             \tag{12}
\]
By (10), the case function necessarily takes its \(S\notin C\) branch.  Its only candidate is (8), and (9) shows that
\[
 \operatorname{fixSeq}_{\widetilde G[s_{\emptyset}]}(C\setminus D^*)
 \ne\operatorname{none}                                                            \tag{13}
\]
exactly when the corresponding ordinary recursive fixing step exists.  When (13) holds, execution of that very sequence preserves (6) by the same marginal calculation as in (11).  When (13) fails, the recorded pair \((D^*,C)\) is exactly the thicket/hedge endpoint of the ordinary recursion.  The \(S\in C\) branch and hence Algorithm 2's selector-hybrid truncated factorization are never entered.

Finally, when all district children finish, the Join transition returns
\[
 \sum_{Y^*\setminus Y}\prod_{D^*}q_{D^*},                                           \tag{14}
\]
which equals the ordinary ID assembly by (6), with the same substitution of \(a\).  Induction over the finite ordinary recursion tree, and within each node over the finite computed fixing sequence, now proves that every graph, kernel, branch predicate, factor, and terminal endpoint agrees.  Input determinacy ensures that no formula, successful trace, or extensional target equality enters any of these choices.  The cited Shpitser--Pearl formula-or-hedge lemma classifies the common terminal endpoint: (14) is an identifying formula on a successful branch, while a failed instance of (13) returns the corresponding ordinary hedge.  Hence \(\operatorname{SA\mbox{-}CS\mbox{-}ID}\), under this singleton laid-back separated-selector specialization, reduces to the ordinary ID formula-or-hedge classification.
